CweFindings.Name: Use of Hard-coded Password
CweFindings.Description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.
CweFindings.Explanation: The SQL server administrator password is defined at infra/main.bicep:58-68 as a literal fixed password prefix [MASKED] plus uniqueString(resourceGroup().id, environmentName). The fixed password prefix is part of the credential sent to the external SQL service, and the suffix is deterministically derived from deployment identifiers rather than a secret source.

CweFindings.Name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
CweFindings.Description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
CweFindings.Explanation: The SQL administrator credential is assembled in infra/main.bicep:58-68 using the hard-coded string a fixed password prefix [MASKED] and a deterministic suffix derived from resourceGroup().id and environmentName, then passed as administratorLoginPassword.

CweFindings.Name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CweFindings.Description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoService.UploadPhotoAsync (lines 81-89) accepts a file based on the client-controlled ContentType, and lines 109-120 derive the stored extension from the supplied filename. ImageSharp decode errors are caught without rejecting the upload (lines 125-138), after which the original content is written beneath the web root (lines 140-145). This permits non-image content with an allowed claimed MIME type and a chosen extension to be stored and processed/served as an uploaded photo.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoService.UploadPhotoAsync (PhotoService.cs:82-89, 109-120, 125-145) trusts the client-supplied MIME type and stores the original filename extension under wwwroot even when ImageSharp cannot decode the content; Program.cs:62-70 enables static file serving. Independently, the upload response includes the untrusted original filename and upload.js:189-199 interpolates it into an HTML template passed to insertAdjacentHTML at line 166, enabling stored script injection when a crafted filename is submitted.
